operations.name: Saw Cut Tube Blank
operations.setup_note: Cut the tube blank to the required part length with facing allowance. The finished length is not present in the routing view.

operations.name: CNC Lathe – Rough Machining
operations.setup_note: Hold the cut tube in suitable soft jaws with low clamping pressure; face one end to establish the axial reference. Rough the assumed local Ø15.875 OD and Ø5 bore regions, preserving stock for finish machining.

operations.name: Pre-Anneal Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Remove burrs from the rough-machined blank and clean off cutting fluids before the specified stress-relief anneal.

operations.name: Outside Stress-Relief Anneal
operations.setup_note: Send the cleaned, deburred part for the drawing-specified sub-critical stress-relief anneal: minimum two hours at 1250°F. This is not a hardening cycle; the material remains in a machinable state.

operations.name: CNC Lathe – Finish Machining
operations.setup_note: Regrip the stress-relieved tube on the established cylindrical datum with low pressure, and flip as needed to finish the opposite face. Finish the bores before the thin-wall OD surfaces; use support appropriate to the confirmed part length.

operations.name: Final Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Break remaining sharp edges to the drawing note and clean the finished part.

operations.name: Final Dimensional Inspection
operations.setup_note: Verify the specified OD and ID dimensions, the finished length, and the general edge-break requirement after machining and stress relief.

clarifications.question: What is the finished overall length of the tube?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the finished length shown on the complete drawing, plus facing allowance for the saw blank.

clarifications.question: Are F03 (Ø15.875 OD) and F04 (Ø5 bore) separate local end features, distinct from the main Ø144.5 OD and Ø135 ID surfaces?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat F03 and F04 as local features in a separate axial region, as assumed for this route.

clarifications.question: Is the specified two-hour minimum stress-relief anneal at 1250°F required after machining, or is it already satisfied by the supplied tube condition?
clarifications.suggested_default: Perform the specified anneal after rough machining and before finish machining.

assumptions.text: The organization’s seamless_tube stock form is used as the available tube-stock proxy for the drawing’s CDW or ERW tube callout; the stock OD is assumed to be near-net at 144.5 mm and the stock bore at 134.5 mm.
F03 and F04 are treated as local features in a separate axial region from the main tube OD and ID; their exact locations and starting stock condition are not shown in the routing view.

The stress-relief anneal is performed after rough machining and before finish machining to allow any thermal movement to be corrected during final cuts. It is not a hardening operation, so later machining remains at medium machinability.

The retrieved heat-treatment sequence is primarily for hardening. Masking, quenching, straightening, tempering, and hardness verification are omitted because the drawing specifies a sub-critical stress-relief anneal rather than a hardening cycle.
